svg.title: 2. Hot shards and partition keys
svg.text: Before: partition key = zone_id (1,200 delivery zones)
After: partition key = session_id (about 400,000 live sessions)
Keep the key but add a bounded suffix,
the 8 sub-streams in Flink. Order holds
KPL aggregation packs small events into
records/s limit, not the 1 MB/s one.
Retry with jitter, never in a tight loop.
Shared reads are 2 MB/s per shard across
all consumers. Give the Flink job enhanced
fan-out (its own 2 MB/s per shard) so
Firehose and Lambda do not starve it.
Why one busy key throttles a 72-shard stream, and how to fix it without adding shards
PutRecords → MD5(partition key) → 128-bit hash key range → exactly one shard
Friday 19:00, a free-delivery promo in one district: zone dub-centre-04
alone offers 1.6 MB/s. Every record for that key lands on shard 17.
100% = 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s write per shard
Shard 17 accepts 1 MB/s and rejects the rest: WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded, PutRecords
FailedRecordCount > 0, producer retries add load. The stream-level average still reads about 76%.
Resharding does not help: a single partition key always maps to a single shard.
Same traffic, high-cardinality key: the hash spreads it evenly across all 72 shards
Stream key spreads load. Flink keyBy(zone_id) regroups events after the read,
100% = 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s write per shard
No throttling at the same 54 MB/s peak: 0.75 MB/s per shard, 75% of capacity,
leaving a third of headroom over the 54 shards the peak strictly needs.
Per-session ordering is kept, which is all the clickstream needs.
Quotas per AWS Kinesis Data Streams documentation; check service-sizes-and-limits for your region and capacity mode.
